I have been growing cotton on these 7 mu for 20 years. I never went to school, but I know what works on this ground. Last year I used 7 bags of compound fertilizer for the whole field, one bag per mu, and I got about 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. My neighbor Lao Zhang bought hybrid Bt cotton seeds from the township dealer and his bolls were fatter than mine, so this year I will do the same. I will buy 2 jin of hybrid seed per mu.

For fertilizer, I will put down one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time. The dealer's bags say they have some nitrogen and phosphate in them. Then when the cotton flowers, I will spread another half bag — about 50 jin — of urea on each mu. I do not read the numbers on the bag, but the dealer told me the urea has strong nitrogen. I would rather spend the extra 30 yuan per mu on fertilizer than risk thin bolls. A bad year means my daughter's school fees are in trouble.

I have a well, so I will irrigate three times: once right after sowing to push the seeds up, once when the white flowers open, and once when the bolls are getting fat. If the sky gives rain I might skip one, but three times is safe.

For bugs, the hybrid seed kills the big worms, but the small aphids and spider mites still come. I spray every time I see them eating the leaves. Last year I sprayed 12 times. I also spray herbicide once when the grass gets high between the rows.

Before planting, I hire the tractor man to rotary till the field. He charges 40 yuan per mu. I do this every year because it breaks up the soil nice and flat.

I hope to get 280 kg of seed cotton per mu this year. The price last year was about 4 yuan per jin. If I hit 280 kg, that is 2,240 yuan per mu. After paying for fertilizer, seed, pesticide, and the tractor, I should have about 1,400 yuan left per mu. That is what I am counting on.
